rows.title: Joined to Papa Stour
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Brei Holm is connected to Papa Stour at low tide.
rows.summary: Brei Holm is a tiny tidal islet in the western Shetland Islands. It is due east of Papa Stour, to which it is connected at low tide, just outside Housa Voe.

rows.title: Joined to St Agnes
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Burnt Island is linked to St Agnes at low tide.
rows.summary: It is linked to the island of St Agnes at low tide.

rows.title: Joined to Little Cumbrae
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Castle Island is joined to Little Cumbrae at low tide.
rows.summary: It is joined to Little Cumbrae at low tide.

rows.title: Joined across the sandbanks
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Ceann Ear is connected by sandbanks to Ceann Iar via Sibhinis at low tide.
rows.summary: It is the most easterly of the three main Monach Islands, and connected by sandbanks to Ceann Iar via Sibhinis at low tide.

rows.title: Some still joined at low tide
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says some of the Cheynies are still connected at low tides. It does not say this atlas island is one of them.
rows.reject_reason: The article says some of the islands in the group are still connected at low tide. It does not place that link on this island.
rows.summary: They have been considerably eroded in the historic past, and some of the islands are still connected at low tides.

rows.title: Tidal causeway from Anglesey
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says access to Church Island is via a short tidal causeway.
rows.summary: Access to the island is via a short tidal causeway, which meets the Wales Coast Path long-distance footpath at its Anglesey end.
rows.commons_file: File:Ynys Tysilio - Menai Staits near the Menai Suspension Bridge, Wales 03 (cropped).jpg

rows.title: Causeway to Lewis
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Eilean Chaluim Chille is connected by a causeway to Lewis at low tide.
rows.summary: At low tide Eilean Chaluim Chille is connected by a causeway to the mainland of Lewis at Crobeag.

rows.title: Walked to from the mainland
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia calls Eilean Ighe a tidal island that can be walked to from the Scottish mainland.
rows.summary: Eilean Ighe is a small tidal island near Arisaig in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland. Eilean Ighe is one of 43 tidal islands that can be walked to from the mainland of Great Britain and one of 17 that can be walked to from the Scottish mainland.

rows.title: Joined to the other Crowlins
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Eilean Meadhonach is connected to Eilean Mòr and Eilean Beag at low tide.
rows.summary: It is situated immediately to the west of Eilean Mòr, and to the north is Eilean Beag, both of which it is connected to at low tide.

rows.title: Walked to from Loch Craignish
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia calls Eilean Mhic Chrion a tidal island that can be walked to from the Scottish mainland.
rows.summary: Eilean Mhic Chrion is a tidal island sheltering Ardfern in Loch Craignish, Scotland. Eilean Mhic Chrion is one of 43 tidal islands that can be walked to from the mainland of Great Britain and one of 17 that can be walked to from the Scottish mainland.

rows.title: Attached to Glenmore
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Eilean Mòr is attached to Glenmore at low tide.
rows.summary: At low tide it is attached to Glenmore on the Ardnamurchan peninsula.

rows.title: Joined to Coll
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Eilean Ornsay is joined to Coll at low tide.
rows.summary: It is situated on the western side of Loch Eatharna and is joined to Coll at low tide.

rows.title: Drying sands to Benbecula
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says the islands are connected to Benbecula by drying sands at low tide and that the connection is lost at high tide.
rows.summary: At low tide the islands form a peninsula which is connected to Benbecula by drying sands. At high tide the connection to Benbecula is lost.

rows.title: Joined to the other islets
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says the individual islands of Na h-Eileanan Iasgaich are connected to one another at low tide and separated at high tide.
rows.summary: The individual islands are separated from one another at high tide, but connected to one another at low tide, (although not to their much larger neighbour of South Uist).

rows.title: Joined to Scarf's Head
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Forewick Holm and Scarf's Head are connected at low tide.
rows.summary: It lies adjacent to a skerry called Scarf's Head, and the two are connected at low tide.

rows.title: Passable only at low tide
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says the roadway to Gores Island is passable only at low tides.
rows.summary: It is connected to nearby Castle Island, and thence to the mainland, by a narrow roadway (doran) that is passable only at low tides.

rows.title: Causeway at very low tide
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says the causeway to Inishbarra is only usable at very low tide.
rows.summary: An artificial causeway links the island to the mainland but this is only usable at very low tide.

rows.title: Joined to the Orkney Mainland
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Inner Holm is connected to the Orkney Mainland shore at low tide.
rows.summary: It is connected to the Orkney Mainland shore at low tide on the opposite side of the bay.

rows.title: Separated at high tide
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says the two parts of Langa are connected by a tombolo and separated at high tide.
rows.summary: The islands are connected by a tombolo and are separated at high tide.

rows.title: Joined to Ceann Iar and Ceann Ear
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Sibhinis is connected at low tide to Ceann Iar and Ceann Ear.
rows.summary: It is tidal, and connected at low tide to Ceann Iar by Fadhail Shibhinis, and to Ceann Ear by Faodhail Chinn Ear.

rows.title: Tombolo to Tiree
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Soa is joined to Tiree at low tide by a sand tombolo.
rows.summary: At low tide it is joined to mainland Tiree by a sand tombolo and numerous rocky outcrops.

rows.title: Tidal island in West Loch Tarbert
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia calls Soay Beag a tidal island. The sentence about walking across at low tide names neighbouring Soay Mòr, not Soay Beag.
rows.reject_reason: The article calls Soay Beag a tidal island. The low-tide crossing it describes is to Soay Mòr.
rows.summary: Soay Beag (Scottish Gaelic: Sòdhaigh Beag) is a small, uninhabited tidal island in West Loch Tarbert, between the northern and southern parts of Harris. The island is located immediately to the northwest of the larger Soay Mòr, which is accessible on foot at low tide.

rows.title: Walked to at low tide
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Tatihou is a tidal island and that it is possible to walk there at low tide.
rows.summary: It is almost uninhabited, and is usually reached by amphibious craft although, being a tidal island, it is also possible to walk there over the local oyster beds at low tide.
rows.commons_file: File:Tour Vauban, Tatihou, Saint Vaast La Hougue 01.jpg

rows.title: Causeway covered at high tide
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says the causeway to Ynys Castell is covered at high tide.
rows.summary: There is a causeway running to the island that is covered at high tide.

rows.title: Causeway to Anglesey
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia calls Ynys Faelog a small tidal island connected by a stone causeway to Anglesey.
rows.summary: Ynys Faelog is a small tidal island in the Menai Strait between Gwynedd and the Isle of Anglesey, Wales, near the town of Menai Bridge. It is connected by a narrow stone causeway to the Anglesey mainland.

rows.title: Attached except at high tide
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Ynys Llanddwyn remains attached to the mainland except at high tide. The atlas island Ynys y Clochydd is a separate skerry of 0.001 km² beside it, not Llanddwyn.
rows.reject_reason: Ynys Llanddwyn is not this atlas island. Ynys y Clochydd is a neighbouring skerry.
rows.summary: Ynys Llanddwyn is a tidal island; it remains attached to the mainland except at high tide.

rows.title: Road impassable at high tide
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia calls Spurn a tidal island and says the road is impassable to vehicles at high tide.
rows.summary: Spurn is a narrow sand tidal island located off the tip of the coast of the East Riding of Yorkshire, England that reaches into the North Sea and forms the north bank of the mouth of the Humber Estuary. It was a spit with a semi-permanent connection to the mainland, but a storm in 2013 made the road down to the end of Spurn impassable to vehicles at high tide.
rows.commons_file: File:The high light at Spurn from the North Sea beach - geograph.org.uk - 5299383.jpg

rows.title: Reached on foot at low tide
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Bartragh Island can be reached on foot at low tide.
rows.summary: It's located around a mile from the shore and, with low tide, can be reached on foot.
rows.commons_file: File:Bartragh Island from Bartragh Head - geograph.org.uk - 486784.jpg

rows.title: Causeway at low tide
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says a causeway to Bridgemarsh Island was built giving access at low tide.
rows.summary: Following a flood in 1736 Bridgemarsh Island was enclosed by a sea wall and a causeway was built giving access at low tide.

rows.title: Stone causeway to the mainland
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia calls Danna an inhabited tidal island connected to the mainland by a stone causeway.
rows.summary: Danna (Scottish Gaelic: Danna) is an inhabited tidal island in Argyll and Bute. It is connected to the mainland by a stone causeway.

rows.title: Joined to Corn Holm
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Black Holm is connected to Corn Holm at low tide, and that Corn Holm is connected to Copinsay.
rows.summary: At low tide it is connected to Corn Holm which is in turn connected to Copinsay by a stretch called "Isle Rough".

rows.title: Joined to North Uist
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says Stromay is joined to North Uist for most of the tidal cycle.
rows.summary: Stromay is joined to North Uist for most of the tidal cycle.

rows.title: Split apart at high tide
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia says South Ascrib becomes several land masses cut off from one another at high tide.
rows.summary: At high tide, South Ascrib becomes several smaller land masses cut off from one another (the northernmost one is Eilean Garave).

rows.title: Walked across at very low tide
rows.evidence: English Wikipedia calls Helliar Holm a tidal island and says it is still possible to walk across during very low tides.
rows.summary: It is a tidal island that used to be connected to Shapinsay. It is still possible to walk across from the mainland during very low tides.
rows.commons_file: File:The West Coast of Helliar Holm - geograph.org.uk - 1438271.jpg

rows.title: Joined by a tombolo
rows.evidence: German Wikipedia says Ynys y Fydlyn is a tidal island joined to the mainland by a tombolo. Wikidata Q15890105 describes it as a tidal island off Anglesey.
rows.summary: Ynys y Fydlyn (deutsch Insel Fydlyn) ist eine per Tombolo mit dem Festland verbundene Gezeiteninsel im Nordwesten von Anglesey in Wales in einem dem National Trust gehörenden Küstenabschnitt.
rows.commons_file: File:The Ynys y Fydlyn tombolo - geograph.org.uk - 1267069.jpg

rows.title: Tidal island in the Sound of Arisaig
rows.evidence: Wikidata Q24638397 is an instance of tidal island (Q555937) and its English description is this phrase.
rows.summary: tidal island in the Sound of Arisaig, Moidart, Lochaber, Highland, Scotland, UK

rows.title: Tidal island off St Mary's
rows.evidence: Wikidata Q30973513 is an instance of tidal island (Q555937) and its English description is this phrase.
rows.summary: tidal island in Isles of Scilly, Cornwall, England, UK
rows.commons_file: File:Toll's Island, Pelistry Bay, St Mary's, Scilly - geograph.org.uk - 1592263.jpg

rows.title: Tidal island off Tiree
rows.evidence: Wikidata Q40850716 is an instance of tidal island (Q555937) and its English description is this phrase.
rows.summary: small tidal island off the west coast of Tiree, Argyll and Bute, Scotland, UK
rows.commons_file: File:Eilean Ghreasamuill and Traigh Throdhrasdail, Tiree - geograph.org.uk - 194404.jpg

rows.title: Tidal island on North Ronaldsay
rows.evidence: Wikidata Q106889522, the atlas record for Rock of Hangie, is an instance of tidal island (Q555937). Its English description is this phrase. The atlas also records the English name Green Skerry.
rows.summary: tidal island on North Ronaldsay, Orkney Islands, Scotland, UK

rows.title: Tidal island on Gunna
rows.evidence: Wikidata Q124466765 is the item on this atlas island. It is an instance of tidal island (Q555937) and its English description is this phrase. The item's English label is Eilean nam Maidean; the atlas name is Soy Gunna.
rows.summary: tidal island on Gunna, Argyll and Bute, Scotland, UK

rows.title: Tidal islet on Gunna
rows.evidence: Wikidata Q124466769 is an instance of tidal island (Q555937) and its English description is this phrase.
rows.summary: tidal island on Gunna, Argyll and Bute, Scotland, UK
